task.description: WF-03 Step 3b: gate the ISS-0703 fix (`git checkout feature/WF03-ISS0703-20260917`, diff against main is confined to lib/letflow/oidc/token_verifier/oidcc.ex). This is a change to the bearer-token verification path -- the authentication boundary for every tenant-scoped API request -- so it is squarely in scope for security review. The change adds a rescue/catch boundary around Oidcc.Token.validate_jwt/3 and Oidcc.ClientContext.from_configuration_worker/4 inside verify_bearer_token/2, returning {:error, {:verifier_crashed, %{kind:, message:}}} on any caught exception/exit/throw instead of letting it crash to a raw 500. Run against INV-1..INV-8 per docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md and state APPLIES/NOT-APPLICABLE for each with a verdict. Pay particular attention to: (1) whether the caught `message` field (from Exception.message/1 or inspect/1 of the caught reason) could ever leak the raw bearer token, a secret, or other sensitive data into logs or the error tuple -- the design explicitly says raw_token must never be included/logged, verify the implementation actually honors that; (2) whether converting a crash into a clean {:error,...} -> 401 response changes anything about timing/information available to an attacker probing for valid vs malformed tokens (a crash-to-500 vs collapse-to-401 timing/oracle concern); (3) whether the change could ever cause a malformed/invalid token to be treated as authenticated (it must not -- verify the rescue/catch path can only ever produce a REJECTION, never accidental authentication). Claim this handoff by setting status to IN_PROGRESS only.
acceptance_criteria: Explicit APPLIES/NOT-APPLICABLE verdict stated for every invariant INV-1..INV-8
Explicit verdict on whether Exception.message/1 or inspect/1 output could leak the raw token or other secrets
Explicit verdict on the crash-vs-401 timing/oracle question
Explicit verdict confirming the rescue/catch path cannot result in false authentication
PASS or FAIL with specific BLOCKER-severity issues if FAIL
